Ten hypotheses I expect to hold, reasoned from how Adam-trained MLPs typically behave; I didn't check them against the tabulated data.

- **Learning rate at the extremes:** raising the learning rate helps most when it is still very low (training is too slow to finish in 243 epochs). It hurts most when it is already high (Adam becomes unstable or diverges).
- **Learning rate and batch size:** larger batches mean fewer updates per epoch, so they need a higher learning rate. Small batches are noisy and tolerate high learning rates poorly.
- **Strong L2 penalty:** increasing alpha near 1 pushes the model into severe underfitting.
- **Width and depth:** extra capacity matters most for very narrow networks. Extra depth is fragile when the learning rate is high.
